name: Matheme — Topology and Harmonics
description: Seven topology mathemes (projective completion, projective line, Riemann sphere, torus-cover-winding, Möbius-Klein, toroidal-poloidal, manifold atlas) and eight harmonics mathemes (whole-tone return, comma, cycle, musical resolution, Metonic, cymatics, perfect six, tetraktys). Source revision dbf3b17; census T25.

text.title: Projective Completion and Changed Coordinates
text.italic: The lines do not meet in the original plane; their completed representatives meet at the named ideal point.
text.body: Homogenise: (x,y) ↦ [x:y:1]; y=2x+1 and y=2x−3 become v=2u+w and v=2u−3w, implying 4w=0 — the intersection [1:2:0], exact in ℝP², with no finite coordinate claimed and no scalar given to division by zero. Homogenisation uses an extra coordinate without raising intrinsic dimension; one-point compactification and projective completion add different boundaries. Neither statement cancels the other: their spaces differ.

text.title: The Projective Line
text.italic: Two charts, reciprocal transition; zero and infinity exchanged by a well-defined map.
text.body: Nonzero pairs up to scale: [x:y]. Affine chart z = x/y where y≠0 ([2:4]=[1:2]); [1:0] is the one added point, ∞ — a projective class, not 1 divided by 0. Second chart w = y/x; on the overlap w = 1/z. The swap [x:y] ↦ [y:x] is defined everywhere, exchanges 0 and ∞, and extends reciprocal — a specified map, not unrestricted division. ℝP¹ is a circle; ℂP¹ the Riemann sphere.

text.title: The Riemann Sphere
text.italic: Ĉ = ℂ ∪ {∞}: a representable infinity point and a precise change of chart.
text.body: Ĉ = ℂ ∪ {∞} with the explicit map z ↦ (2x/(r²+1), 2y/(r²+1), (r²−1)/(r²+1)); the squared coordinates sum to 1. ∞ lands at the north pole, 0 at the south, 1 at (1,0,0); the second coordinate w = 1/z covers ∞, transition holomorphic. Reciprocal exchanges 0 and ∞ — [x:y] ↦ [y:x], no undefined zero pair — without giving 0/0 a value. Sphere and torus are different constructions: simply connected against two independent generators.

text.title: Torus, Covering, Winding and Retained Displacement
text.italic: Local closure, global difference: the lift keeps the integer the surface address loses.
text.body: (x,y) ∼ (x+m,y+n): T² = ℝ²/ℤ², the glued square aba⁻¹b⁻¹, χ = 1−2+1 = 0; generators a(t)=[t,0], b(t)=[0,t] — four sides, two implicate generators, the native 4+2. The loop γ(t)=[2t,−t] closes below while its lift ends at (2,−1); concatenation adds displacements: π₁(T²) ≅ ℤ×ℤ. Flow (1, 2/3) closes with winding (3,2); (1,√2) is dense — approaching every point, passing through none. The quotient gives ∞/0 its carrier: identification addresses while representatives remain infinite.

text.title: Möbius and Klein: Orientation through Return
text.italic: One pass reverses; two restore — inversion-capacity inside Syn, with its condition stated.
text.body: (x,t) ∼ (x+1,−t): the centre-line loop returns while the transverse arrow reverses; two passes restore it. On ℝ², a(x,y)=(x+1,−y), b(x,y)=(x,y+1): aba⁻¹ = b⁻¹, the Klein relation; reversal follows the parity of the a-exponent, det −1 against +1. The orientation-preserving subgroup a², b gives a torus mapping two-to-one onto the bottle — two sheets, two local orientations — distinct from the plane's infinite cover of the torus.

text.title: Toroidal and Poloidal Circulation — Magnetic Confinement
text.italic: Movement sustained through differentiated directions, with the conditions of its return made explicit.
text.body: X(θ,φ): φ toroidal, θ poloidal; scale factors r and R+r·cosθ. The helix θ = φ/2 needs direction ratio r/(2(R+r·cosθ)) — 1/8 to 1/4 for R=3, r=1 — closing after φ=4π: two toroidal turns, one poloidal. The apparatus is distinct: TF coils, plasma current, solenoid, PF coils, their combination helical (Moreau, ITER). The particle's Lorentz helix m·dv = Q·v×B is not the field line's helix; d/dt(½m|v|²) = 0 by the perpendicular force, not the surface's genus.

text.title: Manifold Atlas, Charts and Transition Functions
text.italic: One space through coordinates whose changes are themselves specified.
text.body: Charts on S¹: u = x/(1−y) on S¹∖{N}, v = x/(1+y) on S¹∖{S}; each misses exactly its pole, and no single global chart covers a compact circle. Transition τ(u) = 1/u, smooth, never zero. At (3/5, 4/5): u=3, v=1/3 — one point, two coordinates, one declared transition. Height agrees: both charts give 4/5, and the chain rule transforms the velocity. Three charts obey τ_ki = τ_kj∘τ_ji; x and x³ fail smooth compatibility.

text.title: The Whole-Tone Return
text.italic: The achieved 16/9 requires 9/8 to reach 2 — the remainder is multiplicative, not a difference.
text.body: Two fourths: (4/3)² = 16/9; the missing interval solves (16/9)r = 2, r = 9/8 — multiplicative, where 2 − 16/9 = 2/9 is another quantity. The fifth over the fourth gives the same (3/2)/(4/3) = 9/8: at 240 Hz the difference is 40 Hz and the ratio 9/8; at 480 Hz the difference doubles, the ratio does not move. Six pure 9/8 tones overshoot: (9/8)⁶ = 531441/262144; the tempered 2^(1/6) closes by adjustment.

text.title: The Pythagorean Comma
text.italic: Twelve pure fifths exceed seven octaves by a small exact ratio; the fit is maintained knowingly.
text.body: C = (3/2)¹²/2⁷ = 3¹²/2¹⁹ = 531441/524288 ≈ 23.46 cents: twelve pure fifths exceed seven octaves, small and exact. Scholtz's second location: D♯ 19683/16384 over E♭ 32/27 — the same ratio, enharmonic only in 12-TET. Distributing it: q = (3/2)/C^(1/12) = 2^(7/12), q¹² = 2⁷. The comma is not 9/8 — but six pure 9/8 tones over the octave also give C: the fit is maintained knowingly.

text.title: Cycle, Interval and Octave
text.italic: Class can repeat while frequency rises: what returned and what moved, both recorded.
text.body: u = log₂(f/f₀): doubling adds 1; the class lives in ℝ/ℤ. 240, 480, 960 Hz share a class and differ in register — the quotient keeps class, forgets height. In 12-TET, step +2 gives two six-orbits; +7, coprime to 12, visits all twelve. Six tempered whole tones double the frequency; twelve tempered fifths multiply by 2⁷ — same class, different height. The closing A♯→C is two semitones with a register lift, not a minor third.

text.title: Musical Resolution of Arche-Topos
text.italic: The system reaches octave return through its remainder; spatial and temporal returns coordinated.
text.body: 3:3 = 3:1 — three perspectives answered by one recognition; crossed with 4:2 it gives (4/3, 2/3), inverted 3/4 and 3/2. The chain: fourth, whole-tone, fourth — 288 → 384 → 432 → 576 Hz, since (3/2)/(4/3) = 9/8, 16/9 = (4/3)², (16/9)(9/8) = 2. Full earned chain: 0/1 = 4+2 = 5→0 = 1/0 = 4′+2′ = 5′→0′ = 0/1, with 0/1 + 1/0 = 1/1 ≡ 100% holding both readings as one relation. Two orbits, two faces, two generators: counted two, never the same two.

text.title: Metonic Cycle and Antikythera: Maintained Fit
text.italic: An exact count beside approximate cycles; the approximation sign is load-bearing.
text.body: 19Y ≈ 235M — the approximation is load-bearing. The count is exact under its pattern: 12×12 + 7×13 = 235. The residual δ = 235M − 19Y accumulates kδ; a machine can encode 235:19 exactly while the sky stays approximate — gearing accuracy and sky-model accuracy are separate. The Saros, 223 months, is eclipse recurrence, not the seasonal fit. Freeth 2021 proposes nine outputs with its uncertainty retained; the count alone proves no gear train.

text.title: Cymatics and Standing Waves
text.italic: u = 2A·sin(kx)·cos(ωt): position and time separate; the nodes are fixed.
text.body: Superposing counter-propagating waves: u = 2A·sin(kx)·cos(ωt) — position and time separate; nodes sit fixed where sin(kx) = 0. Ends require k = nπ/L, so f_n = nc/(2L); for n=3 exactly four nodes and three antinodes — the count comes from the mode, not from any 8+4 architecture. A mode, a driven response and a plate pattern are three different physical accounts; the proposed anchor mapping is an Offered design with its discriminating test stated.

text.title: Perfect Six
text.italic: 1+2+3 = 6 and 1×2×3 = 6: the operators, not the numeral, carry the distinction.
text.body: Proper divisors of 6: exactly 1, 2, 3; their sum 1+2+3 = 6 — the smallest perfect number (below it the sums are 0, 1, 1, 3, 1). The same triple multiplies to 6; 28 divides otherwise. Zero enters twice: 0+1+2+3 = 6 beside 0×1×2×3 = 0 — the additive identity permits, the absorber dissolves. Modulo 6, 6 ≡ 0 is a quotient operation, not a change of integer. 2+2² = 6 and 1+2+3 = 6 coincide under distinct constructions.

text.title: Tetraktys and the 3–4–5 Triangle
text.italic: Triangular ten, right-triangle six, and the two readings of 16/9 — each with its counting rule.
text.body: Rows 1, 2, 3, 4: 1+2+3+4 = 10, the finite sum n(n+1)/2 diagrammed. The 3–4–5 triangle: legs 4 and 3, hypotenuse 5, area 6, perimeter 12 — where 16+9 = 25 counts squared lengths, not leg lengths. The ratio read twice: 16/9 = (4·4)/(3·3) = 2⁴/3², factor counts 4 and 6, structural content 10. The flip holds only in the numerator: 4² = 2⁴ = 16, while 3² = 9 and 2³ = 8 differ.
